# Daily late-winner proof: independently frozen fixture recipe

Source-only Set78 plan, 2026-11-20. Root owns producer execution and all runtime.
This reference composes published Set76 fixture identities with the independently
qualified Set78 kernel reservation. It produces no signatures, mined proofs,
txids or test outcomes. Both actual and controlled-kernel expectations derive
from exact fractions; their different transaction fees/rewards stay separate.

## Fixed original composition

Fresh Source2 uses8 works,8 submissions,64MiB; Round2 uses8 rounds,32MiB;
daily Config2 uses8 credits,6 batches and exactly two native destinations. These
are the oracle's kernel profile, whose ordinary maximum is2 and reserved worst
case is N=R=3. They are selected root limits, not a manually lowered intake cap.

bindings must match before attaching the original paused daily controller.

Reuse the immutable public zero256 wallet derivation and published synthetic

Derive a new fixture wallet-owner ID and pool bearer tokens from the explicit

The production public credential/TLS/runtime layer is outside this proof. A

Store and normal node evidence as Set76. No official/private user key, public

Mine one bootstrap block before requesting any pool template. Bootstrap-generated
rewards pay a separate published fixture address and never enter the credited
pool source. Overall actual context is900s; outer runner1080s
includes cleanup. Fail before effects within900s of UTC midnight and fail if the
selected day changes. No settlement/node/job clock setter or second day exists.

1. Original A job belongs to Gym1. Find one canonical winning nonce within64

4. Fully close/join the original pool/round/ledger/backend/wallet/authority

The nonce search does not submit skipped candidates or loop until a lucky
receipt history occurs. Failed/unknown actions are not blindly retried. Exact
saved-row recovery is the only receipt retry. All uncertainty retains original
owners and fixture paths; no test TempDir removes an uncertain tree. Failure
reports preserve phase/count/send/cleanup evidence without exposing fixture
private files. The outer owner joins every process and rechecks source/profile
and public artifacts on success and failure.

## Economics and public report semantics

The producer derives A fee from the inherited independent native shape and
1000 atoms/kvB, then derives B reward from subsidy plus that fee. Round2's two
equal-difficulty shares each receive half the reward, with99/100 applied once.
It emits reduced fractions for both lifetime gross earnings and outstanding
claims, operator earned fee and residual fee claims, exact A output/change, and
the complete final conditional frontier conservation equation.

`Balance.Confirmed` is **gross net earnings minus Paid**, and still includes any
Reserved amount. A pending report therefore has Gym1 Confirmed=Reserved=A net,
Paid=0 and Available=0. After A is observed in B, its Paid increases and its
Confirmed/Reserved become zero before B's credit. At B60, each gym's Confirmed
is only its B net half; Gym1's lifetime gross also includes A and its Paid remains
A net. Both Reserved and Available are zero. The same-day import's report state
is complete/reason `daily-batch-complete`; that reason also appears for both
nonzero outstanding balances. Prove B immaturity separately rather than expect
an `immature` display reason that current same-day precedence overrides.

The kernel side output uses the existing controlled-backend fee1000, and its B
template excludes A. It independently derives B from the unchanged1e9 subsidy,
not actual subsidy-plus-fee, and labels controlled node/funding observations.
It tests cross-owner reservation/reopen/exact retry and pending A immutability,
not real expiry, mining, mempool inclusion or wallet custody.

This finite derived2→3 case proves the selected canonical exception and one
credit without advancing or changing A. It does not cross physical capacity,
prove an unlimited old-job service, qualify scheduled public TLS operation, or
waive D84/backlog, signed-publication or outbox limits.
